sources.note: Nothing about Kabalai prosody. The chapter's only prosodic remark is general and diachronic: reduced contextual forms arose 'sous la pression d'un accent syntactique fort' and became the surviving forms 'notamment les langues du groupe central' (p. 159) -- a claim about Central Chadic word-shape erosion, not about Kabalai, and not a word-stress rule for any named language. Kabalai's one cited form (bayi 'five') is given without tone marks. Searched the extracted text for ton/tons/tonal/accent/kabala: two table hits and the p. 159 sentence only.

sources.note: Record + secondhand data: a maîtrise thesis describing the Kabalay verbal system on a corpus of 320 verbs (verbal noun, perfective, imperative forms); Roberts 2025 Table 8 reproduces Selgue's forms fully tone-marked with three heights -- low (bàr 'insult'), mid (bōl 'get pale', sə̄m 'whip'), high (nín 'wander', verbal-noun suffix -ə́) -- so the mémoire transcribes Kabalay as a tone language with at least H, M, L marks; whether it states the tone inventory or tonal aspect morphology is unseen.
sources.venue: Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de N'Djaména
